data.content_ref: inline:The target conflates 'preference for higher empirical content' (a purely logical, non-inductive property) with 'preference for better-corroborated theories' (which inherently weights past test-survival). Higher empirical content alone, considered a priori, maximizes exposure to falsification. But preferring a theory BECAUSE it has already survived tests (i.e., is better corroborated) treats past performance as relevant to present methodological choice — which is an inductive inference the Popperian framework cannot license. The mechanism's justification that this is 'the only way to learn faster' presupposes that past corroboration predicts future epistemic fruitfulness, smuggling in exactly the expectation that 'the future will resemble the past' that the first countercondition says would be fatal. The defense thus collapses on its own declared counterconditions.
